learning: Iteration 10 confirmed that ±0.08 m at y=0.07 m drops s-bend progress to 0.04 and scores 35.98. Iteration 8 remains the best proven layout, and no untested change is made for the final race.
notes: Final-iteration package: the iteration 8 design, unchanged. It is the best raced design (56.40) and the ±0.08 m spread alternative was already shown to be worse (iteration 10, 35.98).
rationale: This is the final iteration, so I am not testing a new design. The Builder's proposed ±0.08 m spread at y=0.07 m was already raced as iteration 10 and scored 35.98. Its s-bend progress fell to 0.04 (score 17.05), and slalom still lost the line once per run. The Builder's feedback request describes this layout as untested, which the outcome table contradicts. I therefore submit iteration 8, the best raced design (56.40), unchanged. Its ±0.065 m spread at y=0.07 m gave s-bend progress 0.1825 with 0.05 line-loss events per run. Iteration 9 (y=0.067 m) and iteration 7 (y=0.065 m) both lost progress or added line loss, so the lead stays at 0.07 m. Iteration 6 showed that wheel_radius 0.04 m brings back line loss, so speed stays at 0.03 m. The controller is kept exactly as in iteration 8 (kp 2.0, ki 0, kd 0.10, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]). The unseen final track is most likely to punish bend-induced line loss, and the iteration 8 design is the only one with a measured low loss rate on bends together with a measured score above 56. Changing any untested controller term in the last race would add risk without evidence that it helps.
